The way we did it here in Texas is with a touch screen computer, a stylus we were given to keep, and a long paper ballot with a non sequential serial number. The paper ballot was fed into the computer, you selected your votes, and it was printed onto the paper in both human readable text, and a bar code at the top. The paper ballot was then spit back out of the computer, and you walked your ballot over to the ballot counting machine. Which you hand fed in without anyone else observing your vote. I was very impressed with this method of voting, as:
1. it made an accountable paper ballot for recount purposes
2. was non sequentially numbered so the poll workers could not easily stuff votes in
2a. the order of ballot numbers would be known outside the polling place.
3. required that you show both state picture ID, and your voter registration card to receive one
3a. the state would know exactly how many legal votes would be cast at the polling place
4. The readable printed ballot allows the voter to ensure that the computer did not switch their votes through "touch screen miscalibration"
5. The stylus ensured that the touch screen would work for everyone, as the elderly have dry hands that may not register touches.
6. The vote counting machine did not need a poll worker to operate, thus allowing the voter to retain possession of their legal ballot until it was properly counted.

The only thing I was not able to verify, but would hope were implemented is a CRC in the barcode or another other method of preventing the ballot from being tampered with after being printed.
